desc: Derive/verify the identity f(n) = n - Σ_{2^k|n} n/2^k and that P_k is divisible by 2^k (verified analytically: n - n(1 - 2^-v) = n/2^v = f(n); each term of P_k is a multiple of 2^k)

Verify residue-combination formulas: self-complementary class contributes (cnt+1)*sum_values; distinct complementary classes contribute cnt_r*sum_comp + cnt_comp*sum_r (hand-checked on Sample 1, yielding 5)

Implement the complete Python solution: parse stdin, compute P0=(N+1)*sum(A), for k=1..24 build residue->(count,sum) dicts mod 2^k, combine complementary residue classes, accumulate ans = P0 - Σ(P_k >> k), print result

Validate logic: independently re-reviewed the implementation — identity holds (checked n=12 → 3), P0 coefficient N+1 correct, self-complementary classes (r=0, r=M/2) handled via (cnt+1)*sum which correctly includes diagonal i=j terms, complementary pairs each processed once via comp<r skip, Pk>>k exact, k-loop bound (1<<k) <= 2*max(A) correct including equality, N=1 edge case traced correctly (A=1 → answer 1)
Review performance: ~24·N dict operations ≈ 4.8M for N=2e5, well within limits in Python; O(N) memory; Python ints avoid overflow
